title: The City of Brass

full_text:
The Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik in Damascus desired to possess one of the legendary brass vessels sealed by King Solomon, wherein ancient rebellious spirits were imprisoned. He dispatched the valiant Emir Musa and the venerable scholar Shaykh Abd al-Samad with an army across the scorching deserts of the Maghrib to find the vessels.

Guided by ancient celestial charts, they traversed trackless sands for months, until they beheld a breathtaking sight: rising from the dunes stood the colossal, shining walls of a city built entirely of burnished brass, without gates or seams, towering into the azure sky!

The soldiers attempted to scale the walls with iron ladders, but whenever a man reached the parapet, he clapped his hands, laughed in ecstasy at an enchanted vision, and cast himself down into the courtyard, perishing upon the stones.

Shaykh Abd al-Samad, fortified by spiritual contemplation and pure intention, climbed the ladder, broke the enchantment with words of sacred truth, and descended to the interior gates, unlocking the massive bronze portals from within.

Emir Musa and his companions entered a city of silent, breathtaking magnificence: palaces of marble, markets stocked with silks, and fountains flowing over pearls. Yet every inhabitant—the guards, the merchants, the artisans, and Queen Tadmur upon her ivory throne—sat petrified in silent death!

Upon the queen’s throne was inscribed an ancient poem:
'Look upon our palaces, our gold, our armies of renown,
Yet know that death in one short hour struck all our glory down;
We built in brass to rival time, we hoarded every gem,
Yet dust has claimed our mighty heads, and stone our diadem!'

Emir Musa wept, touched by the solemn transience of worldly power. He gathered the Solomon’s brass jars from the coastal lake, returned to Damascus, resigned his military command, and spent his remaining years in contemplation and humble service, having learned that earthly glory is a passing shadow.
moral: The ruins of ancient empires speak an eternal truth: righteousness alone outlasts stone and brass.
